title: Assign Cookies
description: Brute force to optimized: trying every cookie-to-child assignment versus sorting both and greedily matching in a single two-pointer sweep.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Each child i has a greed factor g[i], the minimum cookie size that will content them. Each cookie j has a size s[j]. A cookie can satisfy a child only if the cookie's size is at least the child's greed factor, and each child gets at most one cookie. Return the MAXIMUM number of content children achievable.

blocks.text: To maximize the number of content children, it is best not to "waste" a large cookie on a child who would be content with a much smaller one. Sorting both children (by greed) and cookies (by size) ascending, and greedily giving the smallest available cookie that satisfies the least-greedy still-unsatisfied child, maximizes how many children can be matched overall.

blocks.title: Analogy: Matching the Smallest Shoe Size That Still Fits
blocks.text: Picture matching a rack of shoes to customers, each needing at least a certain size to fit comfortably. Giving each customer the SMALLEST shoe that still fits them, processing customers from least to most demanding, saves the larger shoes for customers who actually need them, maximizing how many customers walk away satisfied.

blocks.caption: Sorting both greed factors and cookie sizes lets a greedy two-pointer match maximize satisfied children

blocks.text: Result: 1. Only child with greed 1 can be satisfied by a cookie of size 1; children needing 2 or 3 cannot be satisfied with the available cookies.

Before trying every possible assignment of cookies to children, notice that sorting both arrays ascending and greedily matching the smallest cookie to the smallest unmet greed factor (advancing past cookies too small to help) maximizes the count of satisfied children.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: If a cookie satisfies the currently least-greedy unsatisfied child, using a LARGER cookie for them would be wasteful, since a smaller cookie already sufficed and larger cookies might be needed for greedier children later.

Observation 2: Sorting both g and s ascending lets a simple two-pointer sweep process children from least to most greedy, and cookies from smallest to largest.

Observation 3: For each cookie considered in order, if it satisfies the current least-greedy unsatisfied child, that child is matched and the child pointer advances; regardless of whether a match occurred, the cookie pointer always advances (since each cookie is considered exactly once).

Observation 4: This greedy matching never does worse than any other assignment strategy, since always using the smallest sufficient cookie preserves the most flexibility for satisfying remaining, greedier children.

This leads to sorting both g and s ascending, then a two-pointer sweep: advance the cookie pointer through every cookie, and advance the child pointer (counting a match) whenever the current cookie satisfies the current child.
Try every possible way to assign cookies to children (as a matching problem), tracking the maximum number of children satisfied.

items: Consider every possible subset/assignment of cookies to children.
For each assignment, count how many children receive a cookie meeting their greed factor.
Track the maximum count achieved across all valid assignments.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Trying every subset and assignment directly explores every possibility, guaranteed correct.
This costs exponential time, utterly infeasible for g, s up to 3*10^4 in length.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: exponential, O(2^m times n).
Space: O(n) for tracking used children.
Limitation: completely infeasible at scale; sorting both arrays and greedily matching achieves the true maximum in O(n log n + m log m).

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why trying every assignment is unnecessary: a simple greedy exchange argument shows that always using the smallest sufficient cookie for the least-greedy unsatisfied child is never worse than any other strategy, since it preserves larger cookies for children who might actually need them.

The sort-and-sweep approach: sort both g and s ascending; use two pointers, one over children (from least to most greedy) and one over cookies (from smallest to largest).

The matching rule: for the current cookie, if it satisfies the current child (cookie size >= child's greed), that child is now satisfied, and both pointers advance; otherwise, only the cookie pointer advances (this cookie is too small for anyone remaining).

The core idea: sort both, then a single greedy two-pointer sweep maximizes the count of satisfied children in one pass.
Sort g and s ascending. Use two pointers i (children) and j (cookies); for each cookie, if it satisfies the current child, count a match and advance i; always advance j.

blocks.caption: A greedy two-pointer sweep over sorted greed factors and cookie sizes maximizes matches

codes.python:
def find_content_children(g, s):
    g.sort()
    s.sort()
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(g) and j < len(s):
        if s[j] >= g[i]:                    # this cookie satisfies the current child
            i += 1
        j += 1                                # always move to the next cookie
    return i

blocks.text: Sorting both arrays and greedily assigning the smallest available cookie that still satisfies the least-greedy unsatisfied child is optimal: if a larger cookie were used instead for this child, it could only ever help an EQUALLY or MORE greedy child later, never a less greedy one (since children are processed in increasing greed order), so no benefit is lost by using the smallest sufficient cookie now. This exchange argument guarantees the greedy two-pointer sweep achieves the true maximum.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n log n + m log m), dominated by the two sorts.
Space: O(1) extra (or O(n+m) if the sort is not in-place).

blocks.text: Assign Cookies is a foundational greedy-matching problem: sort both sides, and always match the smallest sufficient resource to the least-demanding unmet need, a technique reused across many resource-allocation problems.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "match resources to demands, maximizing satisfied demands", think: sort both, greedily match the smallest sufficient resource to the least-demanding need.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The exponential brute force is infeasible at scale; the sort-and-greedy-match approach runs in O(n log n + m log m) time and O(1) extra space, the standard efficient solution.

items: Pattern: sort both sides, greedily match the smallest sufficient resource to the least-demanding unmet need.
Core Idea: two pointers over sorted greed factors and cookie sizes; match and advance both on success, otherwise just advance the cookie pointer.
Time: exponential for trying every assignment, O(n log n + m log m) for the optimized sort-and-sweep.
Most Important Observation: using the smallest sufficient cookie for the least-greedy child is never worse than any alternative assignment.
Interview Difficulty: a foundational, accessible greedy-matching problem.
One line memory trick: sort both; match smallest sufficient cookie to least-greedy child, advance accordingly.
